neighbours.label: A modifier in the slot right before a word for companies: '⟦multinational⟧ companies', 'big ⟦pharmaceutical⟧ firms', '⟦Japanese⟧ corporations'. The output direction writes ' companies', ' corporations', ' firms'; the same modifiers before non-business nouns are weaker.
fire: After graduating she took a job with one of the largest multinational companies in Singapore.
Tax rules were rewritten to stop multinational corporations from shifting profits abroad.
The port depends heavily on orders from German manufacturing firms.
Several multinational companies have moved their regional offices to Dublin.
The lawsuit names four big tobacco companies as defendants.
Small suppliers struggle to negotiate with giant multinational retailers.
Much of the research is funded by American technology corporations.
He advises multinational firms on how to enter the Brazilian market.
quiet: After graduating she took a room in one of the largest student houses in Singapore.
School rules were rewritten to stop older pupils from skipping lessons.
The port depends heavily on weather from the North Sea.
Several migrating geese have moved their nesting grounds to Dublin.
The recipe names four big tomatoes as ingredients.
Small children struggle to keep up with giant leaping kangaroos.
Much of the forest is covered by American chestnut trees.
He teaches swimming lessons on how to enter the water safely.

notes: Card: ' multinational' x7, ' Japanese', ' big', ' with'; logit effect companies/corporations/firms. Probe: 'large multinational companies' 0.98, 'big pharmaceutical firms' 0.58, 'Japanese corporations' 0.53; 'large multicultural cities' 0.30, 'Japanese islands' 0.08, 'agreement with the provincial government' 0.33 (so near misses may leak).
